8 Unique Things to Do in Shanghai Only
Shanghai is a modern metropolis preserving traditional Chinese characteristics. The diverse and rich culture endows her unique charm everywhere and providing its tourists many unique things to do in Shanghai only. Below are top 8 of them to help you have a memorable trip in Shanghai. 
1  
Huangpu River Night Cruise
99% visitors to Shanghai will enjoy a cruise on its mother river, Huangpu River to see Western Style Building Clusters on the Bund and dense skyscrapers in Lujiazui. For a more unique Shanghai experience, you are recommended to take the Huangpu River night cruise. At night, the lights on both sides of the Huangpu River are shining and brilliant, making the buildings more attracting. It is the one of the most beautiful night views of Shanghai. In general, the duration of night cruise is about 90 minutes with the route of Shiliupu Wharf - Binjiang Avenue - Oriental Pearl Tower - International Convention Center - North Bund - Waibaidu Bridge - Western Style Building Clusters - Shiliupu Wharf. 
 Recommended Tour:  3 Days Shanghai Private Tour with Hotel from $509
 Huangpu River Cruise Booking
2 
Observation Deck in Shanghai Tower
As a metropolis abundant in skyscrapers, it must be a unique thing to do in Shanghai to climb up to one of them and have a panorama of the city. Observation Deck in Shanghai Tower, the world’s highest indoor observation deck, is one of the popular sites to gain such Shanghai unique experience. The observation deck is located at the 118th floor with the height of 546 meters (1,791 feet). Here, you can overlook the Oriental Pearl Tower & Jinmao Tower & World Financial Center in 360 degrees. After arriving at its bottom, you can directly take the express elevator to the 118F within 55 seconds. There is also a ‘Sky Post Office’ on observation deck, where you can choose characteristic postcards and send them to your relatives and friends. 
3 
'World Architecture Expo’ on the Bund
Due to its colonial history, the Bund gathers many western style buildings. Between the Waibaidu Bridge in the north and East Jinling Road in the East, there are 52 buildings of various styles, such as the Custom Building, Fairmont Peach Hotel and HSBC Building. Although these buildings came from different architects with different styles, they stand there one by one harmoniously to show the different beauty of Shanghai. Strolling along it, you are like visiting ‘World Architecture Expo’, being a very unique Shanghai experience. 
 Recommended Tour:  1 Day Shanghai Tour from $109
4 
Shanghai International Circuit
Going to the International Circuit in Shanghai will bring you unique experience in the whole life. You can watch world’s highest level F1 race. Every year, there would be more than 15 races from March to October. Lewis Hamilton from Mercedes AMG F1 Team, Daniel Ricciardo from Aston Martin Red Bull F1 Team, Fernando Alonso from Scuderia Ferrari F1 Team and other famous racing drivers are usually involved in the chase for the championships. If you want to experience the fun of being a racer and get close to the F1 racing motors, you can join in a test drive provided by Shanghai International Circuit. 
5 
Stroll along Old Narrow Alleys Lined with Shikumen Residence
When visiting Shanghai, the first impression of many people is high-rise buildings. In fact, Shikumen Residence in old narrow alleys is also an important part of Shanghai. Shikumen Residence is actually an old style Shanghai folk house combining architecture styles of southern China and western countries. It cannot be seen anywhere else in the world. It is also a good place to explore more profound cultural heritages and regional customs of Shanghai. Hence, strolling along old narrow alleys and watch Shikumen Residence is one of unique things to do in Shanghai. The areas gather most Shikumen residences include Tianzifang, Xintiandi, Bugaoli, Zhangyuan, and Jingyunli.
6 
Experience the Speed of Maglev Train
Maglev train in Shanghai is the fastest land transport tool in the whole world, and no doubt one of the unique things to do in Shanghai. With the highest speed of 430km/h (267 mph), it only takes about 8 minutes on the way between Shanghai Pudong Airport (PVG) and Longyang Road Metro Station, which brings a lot of convenience to passengers. The fast speed will leave you a deep impression and exciting experience. For tourists who landing at Pudong Airport, it is suggested to take Maglev Train to Longyang Road Station first and then transfer to metro line 2 to other parts of Shanghai easily, including East Nanjing Road and the Bund.
7 
Customize a Hand-Made Cheongsam
During the Shanghai trip, do you want to buy some special souvenirs? Then you can tailor-make a hand-made Cheongsam. Even after you go back home, this Shanghai unique experience will be refreshed every time you wear it. The masters of some shops in Shanghai have been making hand-made cheongsam for decades. From fabrics, workmanship and tailoring, each cheongsam is individually designed for each customer. Many hand-made cheongsam shops are located at North Shaanxi Road and South Maoming Road, the so-called ‘Cheongsam Streets’. Shanghai Shiliupu Fabric Market is a recommended choice for people who seek for reasonable prices.
8 
Overlook Night Scenery on Flair Rooftop
Flair Rooftop is a sky bar and restaurant, located on the 88F of the Ritz Carlton Shanghai Hotel. Here, impressive scenery and colorful night views of the Bund and Pudong area can be easily captured. When the weather is fine, you can sit on the outdoor terrace, blow breeze, enjoy the scenery with the company of the delicious food or a glass of wine, a very unique thing to do in Shanghai.  Read more:

How to Buy Shanghai Train Tickets
1. From TravelChinaGuide by clicking the arrival destinations in the table above or using the search box on this page top. This is the most convenient way. 
2. From any railway station in mainland China, including the four in Shanghai. Remember to bring your passport, as real-name ticket policy is strictly implemented.
3. From ticket offices scattering all over China, even in some suburban areas. 
4. From the 12306.cn. This is the official website of China Railway Corporation, but you need a Chinese phone number to log in.
Tip: It is better to book the tickets in advance, especially during the peak travel time, such as  National Day and Chinese New Year. Because there is a great possibility that they will be sold out in minutes once available. Location Map of Railway Stations in Shanghai Four main railway stations are avaiable in the city center:
Shanghai Railway Station
Located at 303 of Moling Road in Zhabei District, Shanghai Train Station is an integrated station which provides all kinds of scheduled trains to large numbers of cities inland, such as Beijing, Xian, Chengdu, Nanjing, Hangzhou, and Harbin.  It also serves the overnight sleeper trains to Beijing and overnight sleepers to Xian.  Video of Shanghai Railway Station  
South Railway StationIt is the southern gate of the city which is connecting with the Pearl River Delta and other areas in southern China. Trains from there mainly leave for Guiyang, Changsha, Shenzhen, Xiamen, Nanchang, and other cities. Additionally, there are many scheduled intercity trains running from this station to Jinshan District. Shanghai South Railway Station  
Hongqiao Railway Station
Hongqiao Railway Station is a large-scale, multi-functional, integrated rail hub with advanced facilities and the high level of modernization. It serves high speed trains plus connections to flights, subways, city buses, coaches and taxis. Currently, this station mainly serves bullet trains to Beijing, Hangzhou, Nanjing, Suzhou, Wuxi, Fuzhou, Wenzhou, Nanchang, Xiamen, Guangzhou, Hong Kong and many other cities over China. Shanghai Hongqiao Railway Station  
West Railway StationAlthough the smallest one of the four stations, the West Station is a modern transportation hub serving for high speed trains, the city metro, and the city bus. It . High speed trains passing through the West Station including those to/from Nanjing, Suzhou, Changzhou, Danyang, Huishan, Hefei, and Wuxi. 
East Railway StationScheduled to be put into use in 2027, East Railway Station will be the second largest train station in Shanghai. It is located near Shanghai Pudong International Airport. After completion, trains to/from Suzhou, Hangzhou, Chongqing, Chengdu, Yangzhou, Nanjing and more places will be operated.

Pudong New Area Facts
Chinese Name: 浦东新区 (pǔ dōng xīn qū)
Population: 5,501,000
Area: 1,210 square kilometers (467.2 square miles)
Location: in the east of Shanghai City, east China
Area Code: 021
Zip Code: 200120
GDP (2018): CNY 1,046 billion (USD 158.1 billion)
First Free Trade Pilot Zone in China
Pudong New Area is a municipal district of Shanghai City. Fengxian District and Minhang District are on its north. Xuhui District, Huangpu District, Hongkou District, Yangpu District and Baoshan District are to its west across the Huangpu River. Chongming District is on its north. Pudong New Area Shanghai is the first free trade pilot zone in China. It is rich in tourism attractions including Chuansha Ancient Town, Shanghai Wild Animal Park and the Oriental Pearl Radio & TV Tower.
Best Places to Visit & Top Things to Do in Pudong New AreaYou may need 1-2 days for Pudong New Area travel in modern skyscrapers, Chuansha Ancient Town, Shanghai Wild Animal Park, Shanghai Science Center and other tourism attractions.
Visit Modern Skyscrapers
 Skyscrapers in Pudong 
 Shanghai Tower
As the highest skyscraper in Shanghai, it is 632 meters (2,073 feet) high with 119 floors. Travelers can overlook the whole city on the 118th floor and enjoy the light show on holidays.
 Shanghai World Financial Center
Located in Lujiazui, it is 492 meters (1,614 feet) high with 101 floors above ground. Travelers can go sightseeing on 94th – 100th floor. And the high-speed elevator is with a maximum speed of 8 meters per second which only takes 66 seconds to the 95th floor.
 Oriental Pearl Tower
It is one of the iconic cultural landscapes in Shanghai. Travelers can have a full view of the city on the sightseeing floor, have delicious dishes in the revolving restaurant and experience the unique Shanghai culture in the exhibition hall.
 Jin Mao Tower
With 420.5 meters (1,780 feet) high, there are 88 floors of the main building and the sightseeing hall is on the top. The outer wall is made up of large glasses which reflect in different shades and colors.
Shanghai Wild Animal ParkIt is the first national grade wild zoo in China. Travelers can see more than 200 kinds of rare wild animals from home and abroad such as pandas, monkeys, zebras, and white rhinoceros. You should pay attention to that spring from March to May and autumn from September to November are the best time to visit safari park.
Chuansha Ancient TownChuansga is the hometown of Shanghai Opera, a gathering place for opera fans. With more than 500-year-history, Chuansha Ancient Town still remains an ancient wall from the Ming Dynasty (1368 – 1644). There is a great combination of western and Chinese elements, such as the Catholic Church which will leave you a deep impression.
Others: Long Museum
Best Time to Visit Pudong New AreaThe best time to visit Pudong New Area is from March to May and from September to November with a temperature of 15-21℃ (59-69.8℉). It is located in the coastal area where the East Asian monsoon prevails, and the climate in Pudong New Area Shanghai belongs to the subtropical monsoon climate. With distinct four seasons, there are abundant rainfalls, sufficient sunshine and suitable temperature. The annual average temperature is 16℃ (61℉). You should pay attention to that from April to September is the rainy season.
During March and May, the peach blossoms will be in full bloom, it is the best time to admire the beauty of flowers.
Pudong Weather Forecast
-
TransportationShanghai Pudong International Airport is located in Pudong New Area, about 40 km (24.9 mi) and Shanghai Hongqiao International Airport is about 30 km (18.6 mi) from the center area of Pudong New Area. Travelers can choose to take a flight to these two airports first and then take Metro Line 2 to Pudong New Area. Shanghai Railway Station and Shanghai South Railway Station are very close to Pudong New Area, travelers can take Metro Line 1 and transfer Line 2 after getting off the train.
Within the city area, Metro Line 2, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12, 13, 16 are available. The taxi charges CNY 14 for the first 3 km, CNY 2.4/km for no more than 10 km, and CNY 3.6/km for subsequent distance. It may cost CNY 140-150 from Shanghai Pudong International Airport and CNY 60-70 from Shanghai Hongqiao International Airport to Pudong New Area.
 See more: Shanghai Metro, Shanghai Taxi
Pudong Food to TryThere are many delicious local foods in Pudong New Area including Sanlin Benggua, Gaoqiao Waffle, Pan-Fried Chicken Bun, and White Rabbit Sugar.
 Sanlin Benggua
This kind of melon is in an oblong shape with a weight of 1-1.5 kg. The melon rind is very thin and crispy. It is famous for its sweet taste.
 Gaoqiao Waffle
It is famous for its well-bedded pastries which are as thin as paper. It is shaped like a moon cake with a fragrant flavor, thin skin, various stuffing, crispy and soft taste.
 Pan-Fried Chicken Bun
With yellow sesame seeds and chopped green onion in the upper part, it tastes soft and palatable. And the lower part is crispier with heavy stuffing and juicy chicken.

Shanghai Weather in January
 Shanghai is a bit cold in January, especially when the sun is absent. Besides, light rain falls sometimes, leading to colder climate. The not very friendly temperature makes January a low tourist season, so visitors can enjoy quieter attractions and more reasonable prices than usual, especially in mid-January.  Beautiful Night View of the Bund  
Cold Overall and ChangeableShanghai’s winter weather hits hardest in January. To be specific, Shanghai weather in January delivers a cold feeling, especially during the nighttime: the daily high temperature mainly ranges from 5 to 13 degrees Celsius (41-55 degrees Fahrenheit), while the daily low fluctuates between 0 and 7°C (32-45°F) most of the time. Besides, the high humidity and occasional chilly winds actually make one feel much colder than the digits indicate.
You should also know that this is not the whole story: there are also some extreme cold or warm situations that may occur this month. Occasionally, the city may encounter a sudden temperature drop, when the daily high and low are only 0°C (32°F) and -5°C (23°F), respectively, and you will feel quite cold. At the same time, cozy and warm days with the daily high and low of around 20°C (68°F) and 10°C (50°F) also exist. So, you are recommended to always keep a close eye on the weather forecast during your trip and bring clothes of various thicknesses. Cold Shanghai in January  
Low Precipitation, but High HumidityDue to the overall not low enough temperature, Shanghai rarely snows, but it rains. Shanghai receives about 11 rainy days on average in January, delivering only 43 mm of precipitation, one of the lowest levels throughout the year. The rain is usually small and doesn’t produce much inconvenience on your trip. Generally speaking, sunny and cloudy moments dominate this month.
The average humidity of Shanghai in January is high at around 72%. As mentioned earlier, this will lead to lower apparent temperature and make you feel damp and chilly.
Daylight Hours & Sunshine HoursWith late sunrise and early sunset, January only has about 10-10.5 hours of daylight. Therefore, you are advised to start the day early and arrange some nighttime tours to get a richer and more colorful trip.
Sunshine hours are about 4 per day on average, not long at all. Besides, sunlight is soft and UV rays can be ignored this month. You are recommended to take full use of these hours, when the climate tends to be warmer and attractions look more stunning, to visit outdoor spots. 
Averages for Shanghai Weather in January
Temperature: 5°C / 41°F
High Temperature: 8°C / 46°F
Low Temperature: 1°C / 34°F
Humidity: 72%
Rainfall: 43 mm
Rainy Days:11 days
Sunrise: 06:48 ~ 06:53
Sunset: 17:02 ~ 17:28
Air Quality in January
Average AQI:62
Is January a Good Time to Visit Shanghai?
January is an OK month to visit Shanghai. 
First, though it is the month with the lowest temperature in Shanghai, you generally won’t feel unbearably cold. And, the climate of Shanghai at this time is relatively sunny.
Second, most of the time in January is the low season with far fewer visitors and quieter attractions, and hotel rates become considerably more affordable. Though you need to know that early month and late month are two exceptional periods with a significant influx of tourists: from January 1 to 3, the New Year holiday arrives, and by the month’s end, students gradually begin to enjoy their winter holiday. Quiet Yu Garden in January 
Third, in addition to visiting those always worth-visiting and beautiful attractions like the Bund and Jing’an Temple, Shanghai in January provides you with some unique and wonderful experiences:
Highlights of Shanghai in January 
1. Feeling the Atmosphere of the Chinese New Year
The Chinese New Year usually falls in January or February, and as early as January, many spots in Shanghai wear festival decorations. For instance, you can admire:
(1) Yu Garden Lantern Shows
In Yuyuan Bazaar, just outside the Yu Garden, the stunning Yu Garden Lantern Festival is held every year to celebrate the Chinese New Year. Various colorful and delicate lanterns in shapes of Chinese zodiac animals, flowers, etc., and illuminated Spring Festival couplets can be seen, showing a vibrant festival atmosphere. Yuyuan Bazaar with Lanterns 
(2) Festival Decorations and Shows in Zhujiajia Water Town and Panlong Tiandi
As the New Year approaches, Zhujiajiao Water Town is adorned with red lanterns everywhere, creating a unique and lively scene. Panlong Tiandi features an array of stunning lanterns of various shapes. Moreover, at both places, you will have the chance to witness festival performances like lion dances.
2. Admiring Special Natural Views in Winter
Beyond the festival decorations and activities mentioned above, this month’s natural scenery also holds a unique charm. 
(1) Limited-Time Flower Sea at North Bund
The Bund is definitely on your travel list. Visiting this spot in January, you will get a delightful surprise: at North Bund, tens of thousands of violets bloom in the chilly wind, weaving a dazzling sea of rose red, pale purple, and white flowers.
(2) Colorful Scene in Yu Garden
Though not as lush as summer, the Yu Garden in January remains full of life. First, evergreen trees within the grounds provide a backdrop of deep green. Second, some trees still bear yellow autumn leaves. Particularly noteworthy is that this month marks the peak blooming season for wintersweets, meaning that you can spot golden blossoms adorning the classical gardens. Wintersweets in the Yu Garden 
(3) Majestic Winter Sycamore Trees
Want to experience Shanghai’s winter atmosphere? You are recommended to take a stroll to admire the sycamore trees. In January, their leaves have all fallen, leaving only bare branches that evoke a crisp and quiet ambiance. Wuyi Road and Fuxing Middle Road are all good places to go.
What to Wear in Shanghai in January 2027?
Clothes: For the tops, you are recommended to wear a thick shirt plus a thin sweater, a hoodie, or a wool sweater as the inner layer. Then, wear a thin down coat or wool coat as the outer layer to keep warm. For the bottoms, fleece-lined jeans or sweatpants are both OK. If you are sensitive to coldness, consider packing long johns.
Shoes: Thick but comfortable casual shoes or boots are recommended to bring.
Others: Beautiful but warm hats and scarves are better to be brought to protect yourself from the occasional cold winds. Prepare an umbrella with you in case the occasional rain wets your clothes and makes you feel colder.
Tips for Visiting Shanghai in January1. Early reservations for hotels and attraction tickets are needed, especially if your travel dates are during early and late January, to guarantee a smooth trip. 
2. Wear thick and warm enough clothes for a night tour, especially when cruising on the Huangpu River.

Shanghai Weather in May
 Shanghai weather in May is warm overall, usually with the daily high temperature above 25°C (77°F). Drizzles fall from time to time, but usually stop quickly, guaranteeing long enough sunshine hours for you to travel around. Scenery-wise, Shanghai in May is vibrant, colorful, and fragrant with new plants and blooming flowers. Considering all of these, May is absolutely one of the best months to visit Shanghai.
Temperature
In the first half of May, Shanghai features warm and cozy daytime and cool nighttime: the daily high temperature is mainly in the range of 20-27 degrees Celsius (68-81 degrees Fahrenheit), and the daily low fluctuates between 15°C (59°F) and 20°C (68°F). 
In the second half of the month, the temperature rises. On most days, the daytime is warm or even a bit hot at 25-32°C (86-91°F), and the nighttime turns relatively warm with the temperature above 20°C (68°F). Usually, at the end of May, Shanghai enters summer, and it’s not rare that the highest temperature of a day reaches around 35°C (95°F).
There are two other things that you should pay attention to: First, rain may bring sudden temperature drops, so sometimes, you may wear a T-shirt alone during the midday hours on a day and need to put on a denim jacket during the same time period of the next day. Second, temperature can vary a lot from day to night, usually 7-10°C (18°F). Warm Shanghai in May  
Rainfall & Humidity
Shanghai in May doesn’t receive much rainfall, which averages about 115 mm. It is scattered over 15 rainy days on average, meaning that the possibility of encountering rain during your trip is a bit high. Fortunately, the rain mainly falls in the form of soft drizzles or quickly stopping showers, affecting your trip only slightly.
The relatively high humidity, 71% on average, may make you feel a bit stuffy during the midday hours in late May. The Bund in Sunny May  
Daylight Hours & Sunshine Hours
Daytime is about 13-14 hours long this month, quite enough to have a rich as well as leisurely trip. For those who get into the habit of getting up early, you have the chance to explore the quiet aspect of this metropolis as sunrise time is as early as 04:51-05:10. Besides, the sunset time is not very late, at around 18:33-18:53, indicating that you can admire the night view and experience the nightlife relatively early, and thus go back to the hotels and have a rest not too late. 
Since there are rarely long-lasting rains, the sunshine hours reach around 6 per day on average, and you can enjoy bright sunshine most of the time during your tour. However, when enjoying the sunshine, do not ignore making necessary sun-protection measures - the UV rays are quite strong this month with the maximum UV index of 10.
Averages for Shanghai Weather in May
Temperature: 20°C / 68°F
High Temperature: 24°C / 75°F
Low Temperature: 16°C / 61°F
Humidity: 71%
Rainfall: 115 mm
Rainy Days: 15 days
Sunrise: 04:51 ~ 05:10
Sunset: 18:33 ~ 18:53
Air Quality in May

What to Pack When Visiting Shanghai in May? Clothes: Generally speaking, the warm climate of Shanghai in the daytime of May allows summer clothes. So, males can bring short-sleeve T-shirts, shorts, and thin long pants; while females can additionally pack dresses and skirts. Because of the temperature gap between day and night, thin jackets or long-sleeve shirts are needed.
Shoes: Comfortable and breathable sneakers and flats are the first choice.
Accessories: To protect yourself from the rain and the sunshine, a parasol, sunglasses, sunhats, and sun-blocking cream are recommended to bring.
Crowds and Scenery of Shanghai in MayCrowds:
Each May 1-5, the Chinese have a five-day public holiday and may travel around to relax. Shanghai, one of the most popular tourist destinations in China, attracts numerous visitors during this period. If you travel to Shanghai at that time, you will see numerous visitors in famous attractions like the Bund and the Yu Garden, need to wait in endless queues to experience programs in Shanghai Disneyland Park, and have to spend much more for hotels than usual… Crowded Nanjing Road in Early May 
After the holiday, Shanghai becomes quieter, but various attractions still receive many visitors - after all, May is a month with quite favorable and comfortable weather conditions. Hotels also become a bit cheaper compared with the first a few days of the month.
Scenery:
In May, Shanghai is a picturesque place with vibrant blooms and lush greenery. Visiting Shanghai at this time allows you to experience both the bustling energy of this metropolis at places like the Bund and the vitality of the countryside in its various parks. In addition, flower shows are held in downtown areas like Huangpu Xintiandi and Qiantan, offering vibrant and stunning views well worth a visit. Lush View of the Yu Garden  
Tips and Recommendations for Shanghai Trips in May 20271. As mentioned above, Shanghai during the period from May 1 to 5 will be very crowded, so it is highly recommended to avoid this time. If you fail to do so, you need to take the following measures to make the trip go more smoothly.
(1) Choose and book hotels that you are satisfied with in advance. 
(2) Arrange visits for popular attractions in the early morning to avoid main crowds. For instance, if you arrive at and begin to visit the Yu Garden at around 09:00, the time that the Garden just opens, you will enjoy a relatively quiet scene.
2. Don’t put your umbrella back in the luggage just because the sun is out in the morning: rain in May could fall all of a sudden.
3. Zhujiajiao Water Town is also at its most beautiful time in May with fresh greenery and blooming flowers like wisteria, roses, and hydrangeas. On sunny days, it is warm and of good visibility, while on rainy days, it is cool but not cold, and you have a chance to see the Town showing a hazy and misty scene.  Zhujiajiao Water Town in May 
4. At night, with the also comfortable temperature, in addition to visiting the Bund, you can also take a cruise on the Huangpu River to see the historic buildings and creative districts along both banks.

Shanghai Weather in September
 From early to late September, Shanghai weather transitions from stuffy to a bit cool. As for rainfall, showers occur frequently but don’t significantly impact travel; besides, there is a relatively high probability of a typhoon striking, especially around the middle of the month. It may not be a perfect time to visit Shanghai. That said, September is a rare time when Shanghai isn’t overly crowded, except around the Mid-Autumn Festival. Zhujiajiao View in September  
Hot First Half Month and Cooler Second HalfTraveling to Shanghai in the first half of September, you will basically have hot and not very comfortable experiences during your outdoor visits, especially in the daytime. Generally speaking, Shanghai is still in summer at this time, and the daily high temperature is mainly in the range of 30-35 degrees Celsius (86-95 degrees Fahrenheit) and reaches 36-38°C (97-100°F) occasionally. On top of that, the humid air makes the weather muggy. Nighttime tours are indeed a little more comfortable than daytime ones, but don’t expect the weather to turn cool: the daily low is at 25-28°C (68-82°F), and on sunny days, the temperature is still high at around 30°C (86°F) at 21:00.
Entering the second half month, the temperature shows a downward trend. Most of the time, the daily high and low hovers around 30°C (86°F) and 23°C (73°F), respectively, indicating that you will no longer feel uncomfortably hot at that time. Note that exceptions may exist, for instance, in 2025, several days in late September still experienced hot daytime with the high temperature of 34-35°C (93-95°F). Visitors in Shanghai in Hot Early September  
Showers Fall Frequently, and Typhoon May OccurRain falls frequently this month in Shanghai: there are 13 rainy days on average. Fortunately, not all of them will influence your trip.
Most of the time, the rain comes and stops quickly and usually in the afternoon, though sometimes heavy. In other words, when encountering rain during your tour this month, you can head to a cafe to take shelter from the rain. Then, maybe 30 minutes later, the sun will reappear, and you can continue your outdoor visit. Moreover, this kind of rain may bring temperature drops and bring a sense of coolness.
Note that the rainfalls caused by typhoons are different. Usually, the typhoon brings long-duration and high-intensity rain, during which you may need to stop your visit and stay in your hotel for safety. Over the past five years, Shanghai experienced three direct typhoon landfalls in September, and all in mid-month.
Daylight Hours & UV RaysDaylight hours are shortening from 12.5 to 11.5 this month. If you have a packed itinerary and want to have a rest at noon, you are recommended to get up early each day to gain enough visiting time, especially if your visiting dates are in late September.
UV index is high at 9 in Shanghai in September, making sun-protection measures necessary during the sunshine hours, which average 6 hours per day.
Averages for Shanghai Weather in September
Temperature: 24°C / 75°F
High Temperature: 27°C / 81°F
Low Temperature: 21°C / 70°F
Humidity: 74%
Rainfall: 152 mm
Rainy Days: 13 days
Sunrise: 05:30 ~ 05:47
Sunset: 17:41 ~ 17:17
Air Quality in September

What to Wear in Shanghai in September？  Clothes: During the first half month, outfits like T-shirts plus skirts, short shirts plus shorts, and dresses are good choices. If you are worried about feeling cold in air-conditioned places like the metro, just bring a light jacket. 
Traveling to Shanghai during the second half month, especially the final days of the month, thin long pants are better choices than shorts. If girls want to wear skirts, longer ones are more recommended. Besides, add thin baseball jackets or long-sleeved shirts in the morning and evening. 
 Shoes: Sandals are OK in the first half month, while thin sneakers and casual shoes are more proper in the second half month.
 Others: Umbrella, sunglasses, and hats.
Crowds of Shanghai in SeptemberIn 2027, the Mid-Autumn Festival holiday will fall on September 15th, and then, three days later, the National Day holiday will begin. So, starting late September, you can expect extremely large crowds and quite high hotel prices in Shanghai. 
However, in the other time of September, Shanghai is in its shoulder season. You can have relatively quiet experiences in attractions like the Yu Garden and the Bund, wait in short lines for popular items in the Disneyland Park, and have a budget-friendly trip. Tranquil Yu Garden in September  
Tips for Traveling to Shanghai in SeptemberNo matter when you visit Shanghai, you will include some of the most popular attractions like the exquisite Yu Garden, the modern and dazzling Bund, the lively Nanjing Road, and the Shanghai Museum with a rich collection. However, you should plan your itinerary carefully to ensure a more comfortable and enjoyable trip.
Tips for Tours in Early SeptemberFor trips during this period, the biggest challenge will be the high heat. You are recommended to plan outdoor visits, such as exploring Yu Garden, in early morning. Then, during the hottest hours from 12:00-15:00, you can visit indoor attractions like the Shanghai Museum to keep cool. After that, when the heat gradually disappears, you can explore the Nanjing Road and go to the Bund to experience a beautiful sunset and the dazzling night view. Dazzling Night View  
Tips for Tours in Mid-SeptemberSpecial attention should be paid to the weather forecast to monitor whether there is a typhoon during your stay - this period is the peak season for typhoons. If there will be direct hit of a typhoon, you may want to advance or postpone your trip. So, you are advised to book hotels that can be canceled for free. If Shanghai is predicted to be affected only by the outer bands of a typhoon and you still plan to visit Shanghai during this period, you may want to add more indoor attractions to your travel list. 
Tips for Tours in Late SeptemberClimate of Shanghai turns better at this time: it is no longer very hot, and the peak typhoon season ends. So, you are prone to gaining a better travel experience during this period.
However, in 2027, if your travel days include September 15, the Mid-Autumn Festival Holiday, be sure to make related reservations in advance and be prepared for the higher travel expense. Besides, begin your daily trip early to avoid the main crowds. 
Travel Highlights of Shanghai in September
1. Shanghai Tourism FestivalIt is a major cultural and tourism event held in Shanghai every September. During the festival, numerous activities are organized. Among them, the most lively, spectacular, and unmissable event is the parade of performance troupes and floats that kicks off the festival on the Bund on opening day. In addition, every evening during the festival, the Huangpu River is illuminated by a series of dazzling light shows.

  Day 1 Arrival in Beijing

A Tour Review from A Small Group2:05
A Big Group’s Wonderful Trip in China1:22
China Tour Review Video from Mr. & Mrs. Moser0:57► Hassle-free Arrival:
Welcome to explore China’s golden triangle cities! Whenever you land in Beijing today, we offer 24/7 seamless pickup from either Beijing Capital (PEK) or Daxing (PKX) Airport, followed by a comfortable escort to your downtown hotel.
► Free-time Inspiration: 
After settling in, relax at your hotel or hang around on your own to catch your first glimpse of Beijing. A 15-minute walk south from our 5-star hotel or a 15-minute taxi ride from our 4-star hotel brings you to the Ming Dynasty City Wall Relics Park, built in 1419 AD. Wandering along the foot of the wall offers a wonderful snapshot of local life – from joggers and families to tourists posing in traditional attire. If you are interested, ascend the wall to enjoy a striking view where history meets modernity: the ancient watchtower, a bustling high-speed railway, and Beijing’s tallest skyscraper, the CITIC Tower, all capture the city’s dramatic evolution in a single frame.
  Day 2 Beijing
Visit Tiananmen Square and Forbidden City; have a local-style lunch and continue to Temple of Heaven; watch an exciting Acrobatic Show; enjoy an a la carte welcome dinner with authentic Peking Roast Duck. (B+L+D)
Today, your sightseeing officially kicks off! Your guide will meet you at your hotel lobby, and then, let’s head to the first stop, Tiananmen Square. The square is to China what the White House is to the United States. As the national spiritual totem, it is on the bucket list of every Chinese, especially the elderly. Wandering along its central axis, you’ll encounter iconic landmarks including the Great Hall of the People, the Monument to the People's Heroes, and Tiananmen Tower. 
Passing through the north end of the square, we’ll then enter the magnificent Forbidden City. As the world’s largest and best-preserved ancient wooden palatial complex, it served as the imperial home and center of power during the Ming and Qing Dynasties (1368-1911 AD). Golden roofs, vermilion walls, and white marble terraces define its breathtaking architectural grandeur. Some say that the palace is now merely an architectural shell. While a portion of the imperial collection was moved south in 1933 to protect it during wartime, with some relics ultimately settling in Taiwan or Nanjing, most of the treasures eventually returned and the Forbidden City remains a monumental treasury. Today, it proudly houses over 1.86 million masterworks. During your visit, you’ll have an opportunity to admire precious imperial heirlooms – from imperial thrones, golden vessels, and rare porcelain to delicate calligraphy – offering a dazzling glimpse into the opulence of China’s imperial past.
Tiananmen Square, Beijing
Our Guests in Forbidden City
After a local-style lunch, continue to the Temple of Heaven. More than 600 years ago, emperors held the Heaven worship ceremony here to report the year’s events to the deity and pray for blessings of bountiful harvests and peace in the coming year.
 ★ Watch a Thrilling Acrobatic ShowNext, prepare to be spellbound by an exhilarating Chinese acrobatic performance at the prestigious Red Theater. Watch breathtaking feats of high‑chair stacking, stunt motorcycle riding, shoulder ballet. A true highlight is the contortion performance, often called the “body art beyond limits.” Witness the artists constantly push their physical boundaries to create a visual spectacle. When you see them bend like bows or wrap their legs around their heads, you can't help but exclaim, “Oh my! Even my back aches for them!”
 ★ Enjoy an A La Carte Welcome DinnerAfter the show, indulge in a welcome feast at a premier local restaurant, valued at USD 22 per person, double the local average, and included in your tour price. Taste the world-renowned Peking Duck – well roasted to crispy, golden perfection and carved tableside – along with other authentic local dishes. In China, true fine dining relies on highly labor-intensive, traditional preparation methods that are rarely replicated abroad. Just sit back and indulge in this luxurious culinary delight.  
After dinner, your guide and driver will escort you back to your hotel. 
Meals: Western buffet breakfast, lunch, a la carte welcome dinner with Peking Duck
Temple of Heaven, Beijing
Taste Peking Roast Duck
  Day 3 Beijing
Visit Mutianyu Great Wall by round-trip cable car or chairlift up & toboggan down; toast to the Great Wall challenge with red wine and enjoy a buffet lunch; drive by Olympic venue Bird's Nest; take a rickshaw ride through Hutong alleys and visit a local family in a traditional courtyard. (B+L)
Today, we’ll journey to the Mutianyu Great Wall for an immersive 2.5-hour hike along the best-preserved and most scenic section of this ancient wonder. As you hike along the representative part from Watchtower No. 14 to No. 23, you’ll notice that both sides of the wall are lined with defensive crenellations. How can you tell which side faced the ancient frontier? First, observe the slope of the path; the higher side always faces outward. Or look for the drainage channels, which appear only on the inner side. They were designed to channel rainwater inward to irrigate the farmlands at the foot of the wall, which is a perfect illustration of the old Chinese saying, “No good water flows into another man’s field.”
 ★ Special Treats:1. To maximize your comfort and time, a round-trip cable car ride is included to sweep you effortlessly up to the Great Wall. If you prefer a bit more excitement, you can choose a chairlift ride up and a thrilling toboggan ride down.
2. After descending, your guide will offer you a toast of red wine to celebrate and commemorate your epic journey along one of humankind’s greatest engineering legends. 
Following a buffet lunch, we’ll drive back to the city center. On the way, we’ll pause at the Olympic Park for a photo stop to admire the National Aquatics Center known as the “Water Cube” and the colossal steel structure of National Stadium known as the “Bird’s Nest.”

評論摘要
由 AI 技術支援
酒店提供免費接駁巴士和星願湖輪渡，方便往返樂園，並可在船上欣賞煙花。提前一小時入園的特權受到住客高度好評，節省了熱門項目排隊時間。房間內設計充滿迪士尼元素，如床頭的煙火燈光秀和米奇裝飾，深受孩子們喜愛。酒店大堂和餐廳不定時有迪士尼角色出現與住客互動，增添童話氛圍。
位置及便利性 (4)
酒店地理位置絕佳，距離迪士尼樂園非常近，可以通過巴士和渡輪輕鬆往返樂園。住客享有專屬的通道和早享權益，能夠提前進入樂園，減少等候時間，體驗更加從容。酒店周圍有豐富的遊玩設施，環境優美，適合家庭出遊。（根據 4 則評論）
服務質素 (2133)
酒店工作人员服务态度友好，专业且热情，能快速响应住客需求。服务细致周到，提供情绪价值，令住客感受到宾至如归。办理入住、行李寄存、客户服务等方面均令人满意，体验感极佳。（根據 2,133 則評論）
設施與衛生 (8)
酒店設施保養完善，房間清潔整齊，床鋪舒適，採光充足而隔音良好。雖然酒店有些舊式，但維修得宜，特別是特色壁櫥床深受小朋友喜愛。游泳池同健身室設施齊備，衛生狀況良好，非常適合親子活動。（根據 8 則評論）
餐飲及活動
酒店提供多元化的飲食選擇，雖然味道普通，但環境高尚，特別是在貴賓樓層享用下午茶及晚膳。酒店內設有多種互動節目，包括卡通角色會面及親子活動，為入住增添了儀式感和趣味。
客人建議 (273)
少量客人建議提升酒店的服務質量，包括改善前台和禮賓部人員的服務態度，以提高入住體驗；加強房間的隔音措施，尤其是針對浴室和隔壁房間的噪音問題；並對房間設施進行翻新，以提升性價比。（根據 273 則評論）

“上海迪士尼樂園飯店”是一座造型別致的新藝術風格飯店，充滿了迪士尼的神奇和想象力。
從抵達飯店門廊那刻起，賓客們便進入了無與倫比的迪士尼故事講述之中。在這裡，身著正裝的米奇和米妮銅塑將讓賓客感受到濃濃的歡迎之意。信步這座佔地七公頃的飯店，賓客還將遇到《小美人魚》《美女與野獸》《灰姑娘》和《獅子王》等迪士尼經典動畫中的角色雕塑。
在“上海迪士尼樂園飯店”有一件別具中國特色的作品：一件獨特的大型琉璃牡丹雕塑，雕塑周圍環繞著經典迪士尼精靈們。這朵在上海製作的中國名花——牡丹。
飯店除了提供包括拖鞋和高級茶包等符合亞洲賓客習慣的客房用品，還鋪設了中國賓客熟悉的花卉紋樣地毯。其他主題設施還包括源於《小美人魚》的“川頓王游泳池”、以《獅子王》的叢林為風格的戲水區“哈庫拉瑪塔塔”樂苑以及專為婚禮慶典設計的“仙履奇緣宴會廳”等。
兩家飯店內的四處餐飲區亦將迪士尼主題故事帶入美食體驗中。賓客們可以在“上海迪士尼樂園飯店”的“盧米亞廚房”自助餐廳與迪士尼朋友們互動，也可以在“絢景樓”一邊享用正餐，一邊欣賞上海迪士尼度假區的壯麗景色。從迪士尼經典動畫《幻想曲》汲取設計靈感，“巴克斯酒廊”將提供吧檯式餐飲服務，而“曼舞咖啡”將供應快速簡餐。

東京迪士尼：出發前先選園！陸地 (Land) vs 海洋 (Sea) 怎麼挑？
日本東京迪士尼分為「東京迪士尼樂園（陸地）」與「東京迪士尼海洋」，兩邊門票是完全分開販售、不能跨園的。如果假期夠長，排兩天各玩一園最盡興；如果時間只夠挑一邊，直接看這張實測對比表選出最適合自己的樂園：

帶小小孩同行：閉著眼睛選「陸地」就對了，溫和無身高限制的設施多，推車動線平坦，爸媽走一整天也不容易累翻。
衝著最新話題與慶典：直接選「海洋」，不僅有超高人氣的「夢幻泉鄉」可以朝聖，還能趕上熱鬧滾滾的海洋 25 週年慶典！
2026東京迪士尼最新消息
出發前請特別記住這幾個最新變更，避免到了現場手忙腳亂：
免費優先入場卡（Priority Pass）正式退場：陪伴大家一陣子的 40 週年免費快速通關，已經在 2026 年 8 月 31 日正式畫下句點！現在想走快速通道，主力就是使用 App 購買付費的 DPA（迪士尼尊享卡）。
門票浮動新票價：一日票成人最高票價已來到 12,400 日圓，平假日價差更明顯，預算有限的話建議挑平日週二至週四出發最划算。
夢幻泉鄉全面免排隊進園：海洋的第 8 座新園區「夢幻泉鄉」現在已經取消進出管制，大家都可以自由走進去散步、拍照或用餐，只有玩裡面的熱門設施才需要排隊或買 DPA。
設施與表演換血：陸地陪伴大家許久的舊版「太空山」已正式謝幕，全新二代太空山與未來廣場預計在 2027 年亮相；接替巴斯光年的《無敵破壞王》全新賽車設施也在如火如荼籌備中。海洋極具代表性的百老匯歌舞秀「動感大樂團（Big Band Beat）」也已終演，娛樂主力全面轉向戶外港灣大秀。

東京迪士尼門票
先給大家一個最重要的提醒：東京迪士尼現場售票處已全面關閉，現場完全買不到票！ 而且市區的迪士尼商店（Disney Store）也早就停止販售園區實體票，大家千萬不要看網路上的舊文章跑去現場或門市撲空。
現在入園全面採取「線上預約購票制」，門票會在入園日前 2 個月的同一天下午 14:00（日本時間）開放購買。兩個樂園的門票要分開購買，門票不能互通！

在免費的 Priority Pass 結束後，現在園區 App 裡的東京迪士尼快速通關預約功能回歸三種核心機制：

👉攻略：【東京迪士尼快速通關】DPA、SP一次搞懂！夢幻泉鄉入場方式搶先看
V妞快速通關實戰小撇步
App 先綁好卡：出發前務必下載好 Tokyo Disney Resort App 並登入帳號。購買 DPA 時，使用 Apple Pay 或 JCB 信用卡 的成功率最高，能避開最容易卡關的海外簡訊驗證。
提早一小時卡位入園：表定 09:00 開園，通常 08:30 左右就會開門放行。建議 07:30～07:40 抵達現場排隊，只要第一波刷進閘門，立刻在手機買下王牌 DPA，雙腳同時快步走向次熱門設施，開園第一個小時就能輕鬆收割兩項大作！
善用單人騎士（Single Rider）：若不介意跟旅伴分開坐，海洋的「印第安納瓊斯」與「忿怒雙神」走單人通道，常常 20 分鐘以內就能玩到，是超級隱藏版省時法。
東京迪士尼開園時間
東京迪士尼的表定開園時間是09:00開門，但實際上大約08:30就會檢票入園，建議在07:40以前抵達現場，不然光是排隊入園，可能就要花上一個小時的時間。提早入園的另一個好處是，可以一入園就開始購買DPA（迪士尼尊享卡），大幅減少排隊時間。如果入住東京迪士尼飯店的遊客，可以比一般遊客提前15分鐘入園。
東京迪士尼樂園7大園區與地圖指引
東京迪士尼樂園（Land）共劃分為 7 大主題園區：世界市集、探險樂園、西部樂園、動物天地、夢幻樂園、卡通城、明日樂園。
V妞出發前貼心叮嚀：園區現場已全面停止發放實體紙本地圖！出發前務必先下載官方「Tokyo Disney Resort App」綁定帳號；若習慣看實體紙本地圖做功課，出發前可至官網下載 PDF 自行列印。
園區設施琳瑯滿目，帶著小孩或時間有限時到底該先衝哪一個？幫大家把必玩設施依照「排隊策略與適合族群」分組整理，照著分類安排路線更省力！
一、王牌 DPA 付費快速通關三巨頭（全天排隊破小時，建議優先買時間）
1. 美女與野獸
身高限制：無限制（幼童需能自行坐穩）
快速通關：迪士尼尊享卡（DPA 2,000 日圓 / 次）
特色評析：全樂園人氣最高、排隊時間最長的王牌設施！乘坐巨大的旋轉魔法茶杯，伴隨著經典主題曲滑進金碧輝煌的宴會廳。茶杯的擺動非常溫和，當野獸在眼前破除詛咒變回王子的那一瞬間，聲光細緻度讓人感動到起雞皮疙瘩。
V妞排隊實測：若不想花錢買 DPA，一定要在開園前 60～80 分鐘至大門口排隊。入園閘門一刷過，不要停留拍照，立刻跟著人潮往右前方直奔；如果開園半小時內看到排隊時間已破 100 分鐘，建議直接放棄現場排，改等「傍晚日間大遊行期間」或「閉園前最後 1 小時」再去排，等候時間通常會直接少一半。
2. 飛濺山
身高限制：90 公分以上
快速通關：迪士尼尊享卡（DPA 1,500 日圓 / 次）｜支援單人騎士（Single Rider）
特色評析：坐上圓木小船穿梭在可愛動物唱歌的森林洞穴中，最後從 16 公尺高的瀑布以 45 度角俯衝而下，清涼又刺激！整個遊玩過程長達 10 分鐘，前半段像在看歡樂舞台劇，最後一刻才急速墜落，整體豐富度極高。
排隊實測建議：第一排與邊緣座位水花較大，擔心弄濕的話可備一件輕便雨衣。如果同行夥伴都是大人且不介意分開坐，這項設施有提供「單人騎士通道（Single Rider）」，常常 20 分鐘左右就能快速上船！
3. 杯麵歡樂之旅
身高限制：81 公分以上
快速通關：迪士尼尊享卡（DPA 1,500 日圓 / 次）
特色評析：由大英雄天團的「杯麵」領軍開車，隨著動感洗腦的電音節奏左右滑移甩尾，甩尾幅度雖然過癮但完全不暈。最棒的是現場演藝人員與排隊遊客會一起隨音樂跳舞狂歡，歡樂氛圍感滿分！
排隊實測建議：設施入口旁就是專賣特殊口味爆米花的「霹靂啪啦爆米花（BIG POP）」，排隊前可以先買上一桶，邊排邊吃邊跟著音樂搖擺。
二、高 CP 值經典必玩（不需買 DPA，善用離峰輕鬆玩）
4. 巨雷山
身高限制：102 公分以上
特色評析：採礦列車在無人的荒野紅石山谷中瘋狂奔馳！巨雷山屬於木造軌道雲霄飛車，雖然速度感十足，但沒有倒吊或劇烈的大失重感，中童以上的接受度都很高。
時段私房推薦：強烈推薦挑在日落黃昏時分搭乘！列車爬升到制高點準備俯衝時，會短暫減速放慢，那幾秒鐘正好能俯瞰整座被晚霞染成橘紅色的迪士尼園區，乘著微風宛如東京迪士尼版的落日飛車，景色壯麗無比。
5. 怪獸電力公司「迷藏巡遊車」
身高限制：無限制
V妞推薦：坐上巡遊車拿起車上的安全手電筒，在怪獸城市裡照亮隱藏的「M」標誌，把阿布、毛怪和大眼仔一個個找出來！全程都在平地平穩滑行，既有尋寶互動的趣味，又完全沒有刺激負擔，非常適合帶小孩遊玩！
6.    小熊維尼獵蜜記
身高限制：無限制
特色評析：入口是一本巨大的立體故事繪本，搭乘圓滾滾的蜂蜜罐滑進小熊維尼的百畝森林。設施採用無軌道定位設計，蜂蜜罐會隨著跳跳虎出場跟著上下彈跳、在風暴中旋轉漂移，細節精美且童趣感十足。
7. 米奇魔法交響樂
身高限制：無限制
特色評析：戴上 3D 眼鏡欣賞結合立體視覺、氣流與香氣的劇院級演出。原本米奇指揮的音樂會被唐老鴨鬧得天翻地覆，穿梭進《阿拉丁》、《小美人魚》、《獅子王》以及《可可夜總會》的世界。超大劇院單場容納數百人，通常等候一輪即可入場，不用排隊很久。
三、拍照打卡與近距離見面會（學齡前幼童家庭首選）
8. 仙履奇緣童話大廳
身高限制：無限制
特色評析：走進地標灰姑娘城堡內部！以步行參觀的形式欣賞灰姑娘與王子的童話畫作、精美玻璃雕刻，殿堂中央還擺放著真正的「水晶玻璃鞋」供遊客拍照試穿，是實現小公主夢想的經典打卡點。
9. 米奇公館會米奇
身高限制：無限制
特色評析：直接走進卡通世界裡米奇與米妮的家！排隊動線穿過客廳、工作室與洗衣間，沿途到處都是可以動手玩的小道具，邊走邊拍完全不無聊。最後能與換上專屬服裝的米奇、米妮單獨擁抱、簽名及合影，演藝人員對待小小孩非常溫柔有耐心，互動體驗極具溫度。
排隊進去見米奇的時候，一路上還能看到超多有趣的展示，可以邊拍照邊等，不無聊！
而且米奇超親切，特別是對有小孩的家庭，他會陪小朋友玩一會兒，完全不會趕人，感覺真的很值得！
10. 米妮時尚工作室
米妮時尚工作室每一個房間都做得很精緻，每個角落都有小細節，讓人不自覺會心一笑。超適合慢慢逛，邊拍照邊欣賞那些可愛的設計～最後還可以和米妮合照。
11. 唐老鴨見面會
身高限制：無限制
特色評析：想跟元氣滿滿的唐老鴨互動就來這裡！換上探險隊服裝的唐老鴨活潑逗趣，看到推車上睡著的小寶貝還會輕輕拍拍互動，模樣超可愛，合影過程非常療癒。
四、家長實測提醒！排隊前先評估的「氛圍型設施」
12. 白雪公主冒險旅程
身高限制：無限制
實測提醒：千萬不要被「白雪公主」這四個字騙了！這項設施的主視角不是溫馨的公主童話，而是讓遊客以第一人稱視角經歷被「惡毒皇后與巫婆追殺」的過程。全程燈光昏暗、背景音樂尖銳，沿途充斥骷髏、陰森森林與巫婆突然跳出來的嚇人機關。家有幼童或怕黑的小朋友強烈建議跳過，真的很容易被嚇哭。
14. 幽靈公館
身高限制：無限制
特色評析：搭乘軌道列車巡遊於住著 999 位幽靈的哥德式大宅中。雖然定位為驚悚題材，但其實走的是黑色幽默與華麗奇幻風格，幽靈跳舞的透明投影技術非常精彩。每年秋季萬聖節至年初（約 9 月中至 1 月初）會換上《聖誕夜驚魂》主題特別版，南瓜王傑克進駐後氣氛熱鬧又夢幻，是季節限定的必看亮點。
適合誰搭乘：車輛行駛平緩無失重感，怕黑的小朋友在剛進門的伸展暗室可能會微緊張，但上車後音樂多半偏輕快詼諧，一般學齡兒童都能順利玩完。
東京迪士尼樂園遊行、煙火
來到東京迪士尼樂園，如果只顧著排設施就太可惜了！樂園的靈魂有一半都在精彩絕倫的遊行與舞台秀上。從白天的七彩花車、晚上的百萬 LED 燈光遊行，到灰姑娘城堡全新的震撼光雕秀，這篇把卡位時機、DPA 購買評估以及表演抽籤技巧一次整理給大家。
1.    日間遊行：迪士尼眾彩交融（Harmony in Color）
演出時間：每日 14:00 或 17:15（依季節不同，請以 App 當日公告為準）
快速通關：支援付費 DPA（2,500 日圓 / 人）
V妞心得：這場遊行是目前園區最具代表性的白晝大秀，以象徵未來的七彩光芒貫穿全場！由《彼得潘》的小叮噹打頭陣，隨後有長達數公尺的巨大花車連番登場，包括《動物方城市》的茱蒂與尼克、《海洋奇緣》莫娜，以及極具視覺張力的《可可夜總會》巨型萬壽菊骷髏花車。整場音樂輕快動感，所有明星角色還會親切地向兩側群眾揮手互動。
卡位實測技巧：
不想花錢買 DPA：建議在遊行開始前 45～60 分鐘，挑選「西部樂園」或「明日樂園」靠樹蔭的路邊卡位鋪設野餐墊。特別是夏天，陽光直曬會非常悶熱，西部樂園兩側有遮陽陰涼處，是極佳的野餐觀看點。
若不想提早浪費時間卡位：直接花 2,500 日圓購買遊行 DPA，位置通常安排在城堡正前方正對花車的特等席，開演前 15 分鐘悠閒走過去入座即可。
2.    夜間遊行：東京迪士尼樂園電子大遊行～夢之光
演出時間：每日 19:30 或 20:00
快速通關：支援付費 DPA（2,500 日圓 / 人）
V妞心得：如果白天的遊行是熱情洋溢，那夜晚的夢之光就是極致浪漫！整場動用超過百萬顆微型 LED 燈，由閃耀著藍綠光芒的藍仙子開場，接著是神燈精靈隨音樂七十二變換色、愛麗絲巨大的柴郡貓，以及宛如晶瑩剔透水晶雕刻的《冰雪奇緣》艾莎冰晶城堡花車。黑夜中燈光與音效完美交融，不管看幾次都會被深深觸動。
觀賞位置推薦：夜間遊行的人潮比白天更擁擠，推薦在城堡正面圓環處或世界市集出口轉角觀看。看著璀璨發光的花車以夢幻的灰姑娘城堡為背景緩緩駛過，照片拍出來的效果最震撼。
3.    灰姑娘城堡夜間大秀與璀璨煙火
城堡夜間光雕投影秀「Reach for the Stars」
演出地點：灰姑娘城堡正面
演出時間：每晚 1～2 場（約 20 分鐘）
快速通關：支援付費 DPA（指定席）
V妞心得：這是東京迪士尼樂園最受矚目的城堡夜間旗艦秀！透過高流明的光雕投影將整座灰姑娘城堡變成巨大的魔幻畫布，搭配雷射、噴火特效與管弦樂，視覺張力驚人。最特別的是，除了《小飛俠》、《大英雄天團》與《天外奇蹟》外，漫威（Marvel）超級英雄如鋼鐵人、驚奇隊長等也首度震撼現身城堡！艾莎在城堡高歌時火焰噴發的瞬間，全場歡

東京迪士尼飯店類型比較
想要玩遍雙樂園，強烈建議規劃三天兩夜。東京迪士尼住宿分為四個等級，福利與價格差異如下：
迪士尼官方飯店（最尊榮、最貴）：迪士尼官方飯店位於園區核心，最大的優勢在於「提早 15 分鐘入園」。
✅福利：
提早 15 分鐘入園特權
免費行李托運（舞濱站至飯店，樂祥除外）
享有預約熱門餐廳優先權。
⚠️缺點： 房價極貴（台幣 10,000 元起），熱門飯店（如觀海景）一房難求。
✅熱門名單： 夢幻泉鄉大飯店、樂園大飯店、觀海景大飯店、大使飯店、玩具總動員飯店、樂祥飯店。
迪士尼公認飯店（CP 值最高、最推薦）：迪士尼公認飯店位於「海濱站」區域，大多為知名的國際五星連鎖飯店，空間比官方飯店大。
✅福利：
免費行李托運（舞濱站至飯店）
免費接駁巴士至海濱站。
⚠️缺點： 不具備提早入園資格，早晨排隊壓力較大。
✅熱門名單： 希爾頓、大倉、喜來登、日航、第一度假村。
迪士尼好夥伴飯店（省錢首選）：迪士尼好夥伴飯店距離園區約 15 分鐘車程，通常位於新浦安地區。
✅福利：
免費接駁巴士直達樂園
⚠️缺點： 接駁車班次較固定，尖峰時段可能因交通塞車，且遞送行李至飯店需額外付費。
✅熱門名單： 東京灣東方飯店、三井花園普拉納。
迪士尼好鄰居飯店：分散在東京市區（如新宿、台場），雖有免費接駁車但班次極少且需預約，交通耗時長，較不推薦專程玩迪士尼的旅客。
V妞小筆記
追求極致體驗、不計成本： 選「官方飯店」就對了，省去排隊時間。
重視舒適度與 CP 值： 首推「公認飯店」，享有五星服務且空間寬敞。
小資族、多天數住宿： 選「好夥伴飯店」，房價相對親民。

東京迪士尼度假區主要依賴「迪士尼度假區線（單軌電車）」串連各大園區與飯店。環狀線共有 4 個車站，繞行一圈約 13 分鐘：

評價摘要
由 AI 提供
此住宿在過去6個月未曾收到任何負面評價。
這家民宿離迪士尼很近，有免費接送服務，早上不用趕時間，晚上玩到閉園也有司機等候；房間窗前能看迪士尼煙花，乾淨整潔且物品齊全；民宿摩洛哥風格獨特，裝修精致適合拍照，還提供免費早餐
服務品質 (492)
用戶反覆提及飯店服務水準優異，包含工作人員熱情好客、貼心協助，例如主動幫忙搬運行李、接送往返車站與機場，即使非上班時間也願意開私車協助送達，且能即時回應旅客需求，主動詢問是否需要協助，部分用戶還提到店家會將旅客遺落的物品聯繫寄回，服務細節備受肯定。此外，部分用戶稱讚店家個性耿直、有求必應，整體服務氛圍溫暖貼心。（基於492則評價）
交通與位置
多數用戶認為飯店距離迪士尼園區相當便利，開車僅需十多分鐘，搭乘計程車距離適中，若從迪士尼站出發前往則距離不會太遠，且鄰近機場交通便捷。另有免費接駁服務可使用，讓旅客不用慌張趕車，晚上遊玩到閉園後也有司機等候接送，大幅提升行程便利性。
設施與環境
飯店整體裝潢充滿巧思，審美在線，環境舒適愜意適合放鬆休閒，部分房型設有露台，拍照打卡效果佳。房間空間寬敞整潔，物品齊全，實物與宣傳圖片一致。早餐種類雖不算繁多但味道尚可、熱乎管飽，店家還會為趕路的旅客準備路餐，部分用戶提到可選擇的房型齊全，能滿足不同人數的住宿需求。
免費服務與便利性
飯店提供多項免費服務，包含免費早餐、免費迪士尼接駁車，部分用戶還獲得店家預備的熱粥、饅頭、雞蛋等餐點，且無需押金即可入住，整體住宿流程順暢無煩惱。
客人建議 (7)
少量客人建議，房間衛生需加強，空間設計應更人性化，並提升服務品質。（基於7則評價）

title: 【上海植物園】被春風翻開的植物圖鑒：上海植物園賞花指南 - Go Travelling World
text:
2026-06-08 晚風輕輕吹上海旅遊上海植物園0 Comments 
春日的花事，宛如自然賦予人類的啟示錄。漫步在上海植物園，攜帶這份“賞花指南”，避開熙熙攘攘的人群，沉浸於賞花悟道之中。
延伸閱讀：【上海自由行】三天兩晚自由行全攻略，交通、行程、住宿、美食
每一株植物，都是身著花衣的哲學家，蘊藏著成長、抉擇與生存的深刻哲理。

上海植物園賞花
櫻花
粉白夢境，最是極致浪漫的詮釋
櫻花以300多天的沉寂，換來7日的絢爛綻放。初綻時，如少女指尖的胭脂，羞澀而熱烈;盛放時，千朵萬朵同時綻放，將天空染成溫柔的粉色暴動;飄零時，則如粉色的雪，認真而決絕。當其他花朵還在追求持久，櫻花已領悟“向死而生”的美學。
觀賞地點：薔薇園櫻花林、盆景園、蘭室、南區溫室周圍、北區等。
觀賞品種：東京櫻花、美國櫻、大葉早櫻、大島櫻等約80個品種。
玉蘭
蟄伏大師，時間之外的孤勇者
玉蘭的花苞從冬至春蟄伏百日，綻放時花瓣舒展至極。氣溫連續3天超過15℃，花苞便突然炸裂，沉默的等待化作驚雷。玉蘭品種繁多，當早春的玉蘭類華麗謝幕，星花玉蘭、二喬玉蘭等也陸續登場，延續春日玉蘭的盛宴。
觀賞地點：木蘭園、蘭室、盆景園、牡丹園。
觀賞品種：二喬玉蘭、星花玉蘭、紫玉蘭等近100個品種。
海棠
跨界啟示，從分類學到萬有引力
海棠自古受文人墨客青睞，其詩詞既抒情又蘊含植物學智慧。古典海棠四品：西府海棠、垂絲海棠、木瓜海棠、貼梗海棠。其中前兩者為蘋果屬，後兩者為木瓜屬，一定程度上可以理解為海棠其實是不同種類蘋果和木瓜的統稱，這是否讓你想到牛頓的蘋果與萬有引力?又是否憶起《詩經•衛風•木瓜》……
觀賞地點：薔薇園、北區、熱帶植物館(番木瓜)、藤蔓園(野木瓜)等。
觀賞品種：垂絲海棠、西府海棠、木瓜海棠、貼梗海棠、湖北海棠等。
牡丹
人間富貴花，極致之美顯霸道
牡丹被譽為“花中之王”，兼具盛唐華貴與植物學精密演化。即使單朵花養分消耗巨大，卻仍選擇盡情綻放，以吸引高階傳粉者。芍藥與牡丹相似，常使人混淆，二者實為“木本與草本的姐妹花”。而荷包牡丹花似荷包，葉似牡丹，卻與牡丹親緣甚遠。
觀賞地點：牡丹園、草藥園。
觀賞品種：中原牡丹、江南牡丹、伊藤牡丹、芍藥、荷包牡丹等。
桃花
夭夭其華，灼灼其姿，偏沾了人間煙火
東風過處，桃花醒來，似將三月春光揉碎綴滿枝頭。遠望如緋雲墜地，近觀如美人初妝。粉、紅、白，各色爭豔。最妙是那將開未開的花苞，緋色羞怯，如少女抿唇藏笑。全開後，花蕊淌蜜，引蜜蜂蝴蝶跌跌撞撞赴宴。
觀賞地點：薔薇園、單子葉植物區、植物大樓周圍、岩生植物園等。
觀賞品種：碧桃、蟠桃、‘菊花’桃、‘品虹’桃、‘灑金龍柱’桃等。
杜鵑花
花中西施，姹紫嫣紅
四月，杜鵑以驚世之美，為春添上濃墨重彩。那漫山遍野，非含苞之羞，而是盛放之極致——深紅如朝霞，粉紫似煙雨，純白若新雪。杜鵑，花中西施，野性難馴，肆意張揚。杜鵑鳥以歌喚山川，杜鵑花以血染春，共譜四月天最動人之曲，演繹生命之絢爛與守望。
觀賞地點：杜鵑園、廣玉蘭大道、北區、亞高山植物館。
觀賞品種：杜鵑花、錦繡杜鵑、雲錦杜鵑、馬銀花、馬纓杜鵑等約100種。
瓊花
維揚獨株，四海無雙
煙雨江南，瓊花悄綻，玉潔冰清，傳為隋煬帝所求之絕世容顏。北宋王禹偁筆下的古瓊花，乃神話孤品，僅生於揚州，後神秘消亡。明清後所稱“瓊花”，實為“聚八仙”，即今之瓊花(Viburnum keteleeri)。瓊花八朵不孕花環中央可孕花，智慧生存之道也。
觀賞地點：桂花園、蕨類園、廣玉蘭大道、北區、盆景園。
觀賞品種：瓊花、繡球莢蒾、台東莢蒾、煙管莢蒾等。
木香與酴醾
香雪海，春日暴雪
木香與酴醾，唐宋詩詞中之“雙生花”，世人青睞，風雅之爭亦相親。萬千細碎白黃，染世界為甜夢。單朵雖小，千萬同心，如香雪傾瀉，金簾垂掛。無玫瑰之刺，卻以柔韌藤蔓征服廊架。花瀑之下，悟最美征服非鋒芒，最動人之力乃柔軟。藤花滿架，乃春之無字情詩。
觀賞地點：藤蔓園、薔薇園、草藥園、盆景園。
觀賞品種：木香花、酴醾、金櫻子、黃木香花、紅木香、重瓣空心藨等。
紫藤
疑是紫色星河垂人間
當春風掠過廊架，紫藤蘇醒了，看似枯幹的藤幹，萬千花穗垂落，似銀河傾瀉，如雲霞停駐，每一串花序都是春天揮毫寫下的狂草，在光影中搖曳，將時光染成深淺不一的紫，詮釋“柔韌的力量”。
觀賞地點：環保區遊船碼頭、桂花園、藤蔓園、薔薇園、盆景園等。
觀賞品種：紫藤、銀藤、多花紫藤品種。
來上海植物園，沉浸式賞花悟道。不妨做個自然筆記，記錄每一個美好瞬間。向花兒學習時間管理和生存智慧，做一個隨時准備綻放的人。
上海植物園入園須知
上海植物園1號門(龍吳路1111號)開放時間為11月～次年4月7:00-17:00，5月～10月7:00-18:00;3號門(百色路940號)、4號門(羅城路151號)開放時間為11月～次年4月6:00-17:00，5月～10月6:00-18:00。殘疾車輛統一從1號門進出。
上海植物園遊園須知
請廣大市民繼續保持安全遊園距離，做好個人防護措施，當好自己健康的第一責任人。
為確保市民遊客能擁有安全舒適的遊園環境，請大家錯峰出行，若達到承載量上限園方將采取相應大客流預案。因室內專類園瞬時承載量有限，遊客量高峰時段，謝絕開展聚集類非遊園活動。
上海植物園來園交通
公共交通：
【一號門(龍吳路1111號)】
龍吳路百色路站：56、714、720、770、824、956、958、178、上奉專線
【三號門(百色路940號)】
百色路龍川北路站：824、720、973
龍川北路百色路站：810、820、192、824、718、973、957、南南線【四號門(羅城路151號)】
軌道交通3號線石龍路站，出站後過天橋，沿東泉路步行至羅城路。
自駕車：
因上海植物園2號門停車場已經拆除，周邊停車資源緊張，請市民朋友盡量選擇公共交通，綠色出行。

title: Lujiazui - Shanghai Financial Center Skyline Icon - LoongWander
text:
Located on the banks of the Huangpu River in Pudong New Area, Shanghai, Lujiazui is the financial center and iconic cultural tourism hub of the city. Geographically, Lujiazui spans from Pudong South Road and the Ring Road in the east, Dongchang Road in the south, to the Huangpu River in the west and north, covering a total area of approximately 1.7 square kilometers. As a core landmark of Shanghai's Pudong development and opening-up, Lujiazui is characterized by its dense cluster of super high-rise buildings, a comprehensive financial service system, and unique riverside landscapes. It houses several skyscrapers among the world's tallest, with the Shanghai Tower reaching a total height of 632 meters, making it the tallest building in China and the third tallest in the world; the Shanghai World Financial Center stands at 492 meters, and the Jin Mao Tower at 420.5 meters. These three structures collectively form the "Lujiazui Three-piece Set" urban skyline. As of 2025, the Lujiazui area is home to over a thousand financial institutions and dozens of regional headquarters of multinational corporations. It also integrates diverse tourism functions such as riverside leisure, urban sightseeing, and cultural experiences, welcoming more than ten million visitors annually, solidifying its status as the core destination of Shanghai's urban tourism.
History and Culture
The name Lujiazui derives from Lu Shen, a scholar of the Hanlin Academy during the Ming Dynasty, whose family once resided here. Additionally, the area lies at a bend in the Huangpu River, resembling a "mouth," hence the name. In modern times, Lujiazui was once a major center for light industry and a hub for wharf storage in Shanghai, witnessing the initial development of modern Shanghai's industry and preserving a small number of relics of modern industrial architecture, serving as important evidence of Pudong's historical context.
In 1990, the national strategy for the development and opening-up of Pudong in Shanghai was officially launched, designating Lujiazui as a national-level financial and trade zone. Since then, it has embarked on a transformation journey from a traditional industrial zone to an international financial center. Over the past three decades, Lujiazui has evolved from an area of farmland and old factories into a modern urban district integrating finance, trade, tourism, and culture. Its development journey is a vivid epitome of China's reform and opening-up, and it has fostered the unique cultural core of Lujiazui—the "Pudong Spirit" of daring to explore, innovate, and take the lead.
Today, while retaining its core financial functions, Lujiazui continuously integrates Shanghai-style culture and modern urban culture. Urban public spaces such as the Bund Riverside Avenue, various art galleries, and cultural exhibitions and performances have transformed Lujiazui into not only a financial hub but also a vital platform for cultural exchange in Shanghai, achieving mutual empowerment between economy and culture.
Main Attractions
Shanghai Tower
Standing at 501 Yincheng Middle Road, Lujiazui, the Shanghai Tower has a total floor area of 578,000 square meters and a height of 632 meters. Designed by the American architectural firm Gensler, it was officially put into use in 2016. With 118 floors above ground and 5 underground floors, the tower integrates office, hotel, sightseeing, and commercial functions. Its iconic "Shanghai Skyline" observation deck is located on floors 118-119, at an altitude of 546 meters. Equipped with the world's fastest super high-speed elevator (reaching a speed of 18 meters per second), it takes only 55 seconds to travel from the underground 1st floor to the observation deck. Visitors can enjoy a 360-degree panoramic view of Shanghai, making it the premier high-altitude sightseeing spot in Lujiazui.
Shanghai Tower
Shanghai World Financial Center
Located at 100 Century Avenue, Lujiazui, the Shanghai World Financial Center stands at a height of 492 meters with 101 floors above ground and 3 underground floors, covering a total floor area of 381,600 square meters. It officially opened in 2008. Its most distinctive feature is the "wind tunnel" shape at the top. The observation facilities are located on floors 94 (423 meters), 97 (439 meters), and 100 (474 meters), among which the 100th-floor suspended observation corridor uses transparent glass floors, allowing visitors to directly view the urban landscape beneath their feet. It is a highly distinctive high-altitude sightseeing experience spot in Lujiazui. The tower also accommodates international financial offices and commercial facilities.
Shanghai World Financial Center
Jin Mao Tower
Located at 88 Century Avenue, Lujiazui, the Jin Mao Tower has a total height of 420.5 meters with 88 floors above ground and 3 underground floors, covering a total floor area of 290,000 square meters. Completed and opened in 1999, it is an early super high-rise landmark building in Lujiazui. The tower integrates traditional Chinese pagoda architectural style with modern skyscraper design. The 88th-floor observation deck, at a height of 340.1 meters, features an open-air high-altitude viewing platform, offering a close-up view of the Huangpu River and the cityscape on both banks. The tower also houses the Grand Hyatt Shanghai, occupying floors 53 to 87, making it one of the tallest hotels in the world and setting a benchmark for the integration of business and sightseeing.
Jin Mao Tower
Bund Riverside Avenue, Lujiazui
Stretching approximately 2.5 kilometers from Dongchang Road Ferry to Pudong South Road, covering an area of about 100,000 square meters, the Bund Riverside Avenue, Lujiazui, is an urban riverside public space integrating leisure, sightseeing, and ecology. Adjacent to the Huangpu River and facing the Bund International Architecture Exposition across the river, the avenue is equipped with hydrophilic platforms, viewing walkways, green landscapes, and various leisure facilities. Visitors can stroll along the river to admire the Huangpu River scenery and the Lujiazui skyline, making it a popular spot for photographing Shanghai's urban landscape. It is open 24 hours a day and serves as the core area for leisure activities for both residents and tourists in Lujiazui.
Bund Riverside Avenue, Lujiazui
Shanghai Ocean Aquarium
Located at 1388 Huansha Road, Lujiazui, the Shanghai Ocean Aquarium covers a total floor area of approximately 20,500 square meters. It is a national AAAA-level tourist attraction that officially opened to the public in 2002. The aquarium features a 155-meter-long underwater tunnel, one of the longest in the world, showcasing over 500 species and 10,000 aquatic organisms from all five continents and four oceans, including rare species such as the Chinese sturgeon and Chinese alligator. It serves as an integrated marine-themed exhibition hall combining display, popular science, and education, welcoming over 2 million visitors annually.
Shanghai Ocean Aquarium
Shanghai Disney Store
Located at 180 Fenghe Road, Lujiazui, the Shanghai Disney Store (Lujiazui Branch) is the first flagship store of Disney in Mainland China, covering a floor area of approximately 5,000 square meters. The store features a comprehensive range of Disney-themed products, from classic cartoon character merchandise to limited-edition souvenirs, making it a popular destination for family outings and Disney fans. Shanghai Huangpu River Cruise: Route, Price, Tips
When traveling in Shanghai, you should not miss a cruise tour on the Huangpu River. It is the best way to admire Shanghai's classic skyline views of colonial architecture and modern skyscrapers along the river.
The Huangpu River — "the Mother River of Shanghai"
The Huangpu River, the largest river passing through the city of Shanghai, is honored as the mother river of Shanghai.
It stretches for 113 kilometers (70 miles) with an average width of 400 meters and a depth of 9 meters. It snakes its way through Shanghai and divides the city into two sections: Pudong in the east and Puxi in the west.
It is also the source of most of Shanghai's drinking water, after it goes through a purification process, of course. Today, the Huangpu River is the site of a bustling tourist business in the form of river cruises.
Cruise Route and Price
There are many cruise options which vary in size, capacity, decoration, and amenities. Some boats look very trendy with a modern-style bar, while some are decorated in a traditional Chinese style. The cruises can hold passengers ranging from 80 to 1,000. You can choose a boat based on your interests.
Huangpu River Cruise
There are several tour lengths you can choose from, from a 30-minute cruise to a 3½-hour cruise. The cruises along the Huangpu River often start from the wharf near the Bund, and head towards Yangpu Bridge or Wusongkou International Cruise Terminal, and back again along the opposite side of the river to the Bund.
At present, the most popular one is the 50-minute classic cruise. The cruises are available during the day and night. It is recommended to take a cruise at night when the river is veiled in the sparkling neon lights on both sides.
Cruise route: Shiliupu Wharf near the Bund – Shanghai Tower – Shanghai World Financial Center – Jinmao Tower – Oriental Pearl TV Tower – Yangpu Bridge – Waibaidu Bridge – Monument to the People's Heroes – Peace Hotel – Customs House – back to the wharf
Boarding place: Shiliupu Wharf near the Bund (531 Zhongshan East 2nd Rd)
Duration: about 50 minutes
Cruise operating hours: 11am–9:30pm
Interval: 15–30 minutes
Price: around 150 yuan (≈US$22) (for sightseeing only, without dinner or snacks)
Ticket booking:
1) Tickets can be purchased at Shiliupu Wharf ticket office at Wai Ma Lu 80.
 2) You can buy your ticket online or through ticket agents. Contact us for details. 
 3) Many hotels also provide a ticket booking service; you can check with your hotel.
What to See on the Cruise
A night view of the Bund
On the cruise, you will see the distinctive contrasts between the classical European buildings and soaring modern skyscrapers from the two sides of the Huangpu River.
Besides offering a privileged view of the bridges that span the Huangpu River, the cruise boats also offer an excellent view of the famous colonial-era buildings that make up the Bund on the eastern bank as well as buildings such as the Peace Hotel, with its unique pyramid roof in blazing green, and the Customs House, with its large clock tower.
On the western bank, you will see a bustling metropolis full of modern skyscrapers and towering buildings, such as Jinmao Tower, the Oriental Pearl TV Tower, and Shanghai World Financial Center.
The Best Times to Take a Cruise
The best times to take a cruise on the Huangpu River are March–May and September–November when the weather is pleasant. You can enjoy the scenery on the deck of the boat and have a great opportunity to take clear and awesome pictures.
If you decide to go on a cruise on a cold day, remember to take a coat. It can be very chilly when you stand on the deck. Rainy days will be a little foggy so some of the scenery on the Bund may be obscured.
Nearby Attractions
Yuyuan: It is a classic Chinese garden with rich history and culture. You will see traditional Chinese garden architecture, and exquisite sculptures and carvings.
The Bund: The architecture along the Bund is a living museum of the colonial history of the 1800s.
Nanjing Road is Shanghai's busiest shopping street lined with top-end shopping malls, old-brand shops, and traditional eateries.
Enrich Your Experience with a Huangpu River Cruise
Take a relaxing cruise on the Huangpu River.
It is a great choice to take a relaxing cruise on the Huangpu River after a full day of sightseeing. Stand on the deck to get a feel for the city, and take pictures of the incredible skyline.

This part of residential area, Zhujiajiao in Shanghai, remains quiet and peaceful though the water town has become an attraction.
Zhujiajiao is a folding fan shaped town, laid among gleaming lakes and rolling hills. It was once a flourishing town well-known for its fabric and cloth industry. At the end of the Ming Dynasty (1368-1644) and the beginning of Qing Dynasty (1644-1911), this place become a rich town, abundant in rice, with busy long streets full of shops. Lakes, bridges, temples, lanes, teahouses and old buildings are all highlights of the town. Attraction Intro: Zhujiajiao Water Town

text:
Home

Shanghai High-Tech Journey: EVs, Drones & Robots
Day Tour to Experience Shanghai Tower, electric vehicles, driverless car, DJI drones, Huawei Store, and Unitree Robots
 Go compare
 Code
 SH33

Itinerary

Reviews
 Trip Highlights
 Take a public ferry like a local across the Huangpu River to marvel at Shanghai’s cityscape. 
 Enjoy sweeping panoramas of the sprawling city from Shanghai Tower, China’s tallest building.
 Be wowed by China’s top electronic vehicles and try a fully driverless car ride.
 Handle the DJI drones to capture amazing photos and explore the smart home set in the Huawei Flagship Store.
 Watch the Unitree humanoid robots dancing and boxing smoothly, and interact with the cute robot dogs.
 This trip can be customized to meet your individual needs!
Welcome to experience the cutting-edge technology in China’s most developed city! We especially pack the city’s futuristic skyline, the most advanced electric vehicles, autonomous driving, and robotics, as well as a local ferry ride in one day, for tech enthusiasts and children with curious minds. Follow your knowledgeable Shanghainese guide to observe how the newest technologies are reshaping the locals’ daily lives and delve into what artificial intelligence will bring. 
In the morning, your private guide will meet you at your hotel lobby, and escort you on a taxi ride to the pier on the west bank of the Huangpu River, where we’ll try a ferry across the river just like a local in an authentic way to the Pudong area on the east bank. Mingle with the locals and take in the stunning futuristic skyline, especially the neck-craning skyscrapers on the east bank.
Take a Public Ferry across the Huangpu River, Shanghai
View Shanghai Futurictic Skyline
After disembarking, head to the Shanghai Tower, the highest building in China, for an impressive panorama. Ascend the 52nd floor to the city’s tallest bookstore, Duoyun Bookstore, where you can overlook other landmark buildings, such as the Oriental Pearl TV Tower, Jin Mao Tower, and Shanghai World Financial Center from the north, and the Huangpu River and Nanpu Bridge from the south. A drink will be included for you! Afterward, descend to low levels to visit Chinese leading electric vehicle showrooms, such as NIO or ZEEKR. The staff will show you the high-tech flagship cars with comfort and rapid charging. If interested, sit in the car and personally experience the passenger-focused advanced vehicles. Your guide will also give you an introduction to the competitive EV market and the difference between these Chinese brands and Western brands like Tesla. 
 ★ Unique Experience: Hop in a Completely Driverless CarLater, accompanied by your guide, you’ll take a driverless car, the Level 4 autonomous robotaxi, in a pilot area. We’ll sit in the back seat, and there is no person in the front at all, except that the steering wheel just turns by itself. It may sound a little strange, but in fact interesting, and you can track your route on the screen. The vehicle was driven extremely smoothly, maintaining a suitable speed at about 30km/h (19 mph), braking gently at red lights, and changing lanes smoothly, not inferior to a seasoned driver. At present, this kind of car is being tested in various cities throughout the country, and soon, it will be fully implemented and work in the downtown areas, completely changing the way people travel. 
View from Duoyun Bookstore on Shanghai Tower
Chinese Electric Vehicles
After the excellent ride, continue your exploration to the Xintiandi neighborhood, the glitzy pedestrian-only neighborhood that has been reincarnated from old 20th-century stone-gate architecture. Step into the DJI Flagship Store here. DJI is acclaimed as the world’s largest and best commercial drone manufacturer, dominating over 70% of the market. The two-story store not only showcases DJI's full range of products from foldable drones to handheld imaging & stabilizers, but also offers a wealth of aerial photography experiences. You can try to handle a drone personally and be wowed at awesome cinematic footage from all over the world, on the second floor.
Shortly after, let’s head to East Nanjing Road, where the world’s largest Huawei Global Flagship Store is housed in a massive 3-story Art Deco-style building right in the city center. In a space of 5,000 square meters (1.24 acres), over 500 electronic products are showcased, including phones, tablets, PCs, and smart wearables. Five major lifestyle scenarios are designed to simulate a fully connected smart ecosystem, from smart homes and mobile offices, to sports, travel, and audio-visual entertainment. You can experience any product that interests you, including the Huawei electric vehicles. In addition, the Huawei flagship store is located across the street from Apple and Samsung stores, making it easy for you to compare the products and concepts of the world's leading tech manufacturers.
DJI Drone Showroom
Smart Devices in Huawei Flagship Store
At last, wrap up the day at the Unitree Robotics Flagship Store. Imagine this scenario: you're shopping at a mall on the weekend, walk into a store, and see a 1.8-meter-tall (5.9-foot) humanoid robot greeting you. Not only can it hold a fluent conversation with you, but it can also perform a boxing routine that perfectly replicates the explosive power of real combat! Its movements are so smooth that you cannot believe they’re robotic. Next to it is a robotic dog that doesn't need a leash; it wanders around the store on its own, automatically avoiding obstacles. If you crouch down to pet it, it will tilt its head to act cute. That’s not a dream, but a true scenario that plays out every day in the flagship store. Here, you can interact with the robots, see how they walk, run, talk, and even dance, or have them do some household tasks for you. Let’s wait and see, and they may just become a part of your daily life someday.
After the exploration, your guide will escort you back to your hotel by taxi, wishing you a wonderful rest of your trip!

Shanghai Geography
Geographical Location
Shanghai is located on the east tip of Yangtze River Delta and halfway along China's eastern coastline. Based on Shanghai geography, It borders the estuary of Yangtze River to the north, Jiangsu and Zhejiang Provinces to the west and Hangzhou Bay to the south. Due to its advantageous geographical location, Shanghai has become a large and prosperous port city. Hereunder are the Shanghai geography features/characteristics: Huangpu River    Oriental Pearl TV Tower & Jinmao Tower 
Geographical Facts & Characteristics
Yangtze River DeltaThe lower reaches of the Yangtze River running through the city bring lots of mud and sand to its estuary. The wind, the river flow and the tide jointly account for the alluvial plain including today's Yangtze River Delta.
Shanghai landform on the east tip of the delta covers an area of 6,340.5 square kilometers (2,448.1 square miles). The altitude of the city lies between three and five meters. With comparatively soft and loose earth, the city has a slightly higher coastal area in the east and a lower hinterland to the west. The area around Dianshan Lake in the west of the city is the lowest. Plains cover most areas in its middle and east part including the city zone and part of Jiading, Minghang, Fengxian and Jinshan Districts.
Hills & Small MountainsThere are a few hills and small mountains in the southwest Qingpu and Songjiang Districts, including Tianma Mountain, Fenghuang Mountain, Hengshan Mountain and Xiaokunshan Mountain. This is another landscape features of Shanghai. Panoramic Night View of Pudong Shanghai  
Offshore IslandsIn additional, there are some offshore islands in the area of Shanghai geography, such as Dajinshan Island, Xiaojinshan Island and Fushan Island. Among them, Dajinshan with an altitude of 103.4 meters is the peak. There are three alluvial islands of Chongming, Changxing and Hengsha in the estuary of Yangtze River to the north of Shanghai mainland. Changxing and Hengsha are small islands under the jurisdiction of Baoshan District. Chongming is the only county of Shanghai. With an area of 1,041.21 square kilometers, the island is the third largest in China.
Densest Water NetworkThe water network inside the city is the densest and the most developed in China. A lot of rivers and lakes in the city provide sufficient water to facilitate the transportation and irrigation. The Yangtze River running eastwards to the sea through the north suburbs of the city is one of the main rivers. Huangpu River, the 'Mother River of Shanghai', is the last main tributary of the Yangtze River. Originating from the Taihu Lake in Jiangsu Province, Huangpu River runs through the city zone. Being wide, deep and never freezing, it contributes a lot to the city's transportation. Huangpu River has many tributaries such as Wusong River (alias Suzhou River). Wusong River with various historical monuments and buildings along its banks offers an important link between Shanghai and its hinterland. Dianshan Lake is the largest freshwater lake in the west Qingpu District, producing various aquatic products.
Lack of Natural resourcesShanghai geographical facts decide that natural resources are not abundant in the region. Natural vegetation is hardly seen except in a few areas such as Dajinshan Island, Sheshan Mountain and some cays and bottomlands. There are just cultivated crops, trees and flowers. The area is not a good habitat for wild animals, so animals there are always domestic. Shanghai also lacks mineral resources and energy sources. Only crude oil and natural gas are found in the offing of East China Sea and south Yellow Sea nearby.

Shanghai Events
Shining like a bright pearl in the oriental world with ever rising international position and influence, Shanghai is a place preferred by many for holding numerous varied events, including festivals, performances, competitions, exhibitions, and conventions. If you can experience one such exciting event, it will greatly enhance your stay in the city. 
 Shanghai Stadium 
2020 Top 10 Events in Shanghai
1. New Year Bell Striking
Time: New Year’s Eve
Place: Longhua Temple
On the last day of each year, many locals and even foreigners head to the Longhua Temple to take part in the New Year celebration: Bell Striking at 00:00. The bell is expected to strike for 108 times, which means dispel the misery of the old year and welcome good luck in the New Year. Apart from that, visitors can watch folk performances, guess the lantern riddles and make wishes before the prayer wall.
2. Yu Garden Lantern Festival
Time: Jan. 24 – Feb. 10
Place: Yu Garden
As night comes, all the delicate handmade lanterns light up the sky and add carnival atmosphere. What may surprise you is that all the lanterns are designed in life-like images with colorful textile cover on. Itching to have a look?
3. The 3rd China International Import Expo
Time: Nov. 5 - 10
Place: Shanghai International Expo Centre
The exhibition includes eight main parts, covering Sci-tech life, automobile, high-end equipment, intelligent manufacturing, medical equipment, quality life, trade in services and agricultural products. The 3rd China International Import Expo remains committed to trade liberalization and economic globalization.
4. Tourism Festival Festival Time in Shanghai 
Time: Sep.15 to Oct.6
Place: along the shore of Huangpu River
Most activities are closely related to sightseeing, dining, shopping, entertaining and exhibitions, fully showing visitors the irresistible charm of the city. Opening ceremonial grand parade, carnival and cruise ship parade across Huangpu River must highlight your Shanghai trip during this time.
5. Shanghai Haiwan Half MarathonTime: Late Apr.2020
It has two race categories, including the 13 miles (21 kilometers) run and the 4 miles (7 kilometers) fun run. Both Chinese and foreigners can join the event. The half marathon should be finished within 3 hours and the fun run within 1.5 hours.
6. NBA China GamesTime: Oct. 10
Place: Shanghai Mercedes – Benz Arena
NBA China Games has been successfully held for 12 years. Every October, several selected NBA teams have basketball matches in Shanghai. 
7. The 21th Annual Ring Expo in ChinaTime: Apr.21-23
Place: Shanghai New International Expo Center
Adhering to the excellent quality of the global environmental brand exhibition IFAT Germany for 50 years, the Annual Ring Expo in China will gather the world's top sewage treatment, water supply and drainage, solid waste treatment, Cutting-edge technologies and the latest solutions in the field of environmental pollution control.
8. FHC 2020 ChinaTime: Nov.10-12
Place: Shanghai New International Expo Center
After 23 years of development, FHC has become the industry's leading trade show. It is a platform for the food and beverage and hotel industries to enter the Chinese market. A total of 3,000 companies from 48 countries and regions participated in the last exhibition. The exhibition area expanded to 120,000 square meters. The three-day exhibition welcomed a total of 118,274 professional visitors, and the attendance rate increased by 23% over the past.
9. China Wedding Expo 2020 Grand Theater Time: Feb.18-20
Place: Shanghai National Exhibition & Convention Center (NECC)
Shanghai International Wedding Photographic Equipment Exhibition (China Wedding Expo) has become the largest and most influential industry event in China and even the global wedding industry. The Shanghai International Wedding Photographic Equipment Exhibition had a total area of 150,000 square meters. The 650 participating companies were from the United States, Italy, France, Ukraine, Russia, Spain, Malaysia, Japan, Singapore, South Korea, Turkey, Hong Kong and other countries and regions.
10. World Travel Fair 2020Time: Apr.23-26
Place: Shanghai Exhibition Center
Shanghai World Travel Fair is a travel exhibition co-organized by Shanghai Culture and Tourism Bureau. As one of the premier annual tourism procurement events in China, the World Travel Fair always insists on organizing high-quality tourism resources and tourism service companies at home and abroad, presenting rich and diverse tourism resources to domestic tourism buyers and many travel enthusiasts.
